slides.title: How to use this template

cards.title: 10 minutes, live demo, then Q&A
bullets: About 1.5 min per slide, 2–3 min of demo
Judges review what you built, not your idea
Report against the milestones you set at intake

cards.title: Replace every [bracket]
bullets: Home > New Slide gives you the Launch Lab layouts
Copy a card or box to add more

cards.title: Plain words, real numbers
bullets: Every number gets its method and baseline
Say what is stubbed before a judge asks

slides.notes: This slide is only for your team. Delete it before the showcase. Full guide: template/README.md in the launch-lab-showcase repository.

slides.title: [Project name]
slides.subtitle: [One literal sentence: what it does, for whom. No buzzwords.]
slides.notes: 0:20. Say the one-liner, then move straight to the problem. Test: could a non-CS friend repeat it back?

slides.title: [Who exactly has the pain, and what it costs them]
slides.body: [How they cope today, and how you know: interviews, survey size n, usage data]
slides.notes: 0:45. One specific user, one specific pain. Give the evidence size (n) and how you found people, because judges will ask.

slides.title: [How the system works, in one sentence]
slides.caption: [Which parts run in the demo today, and which are not built yet]
slides.notes: 1:15. Black box = working, grey box with red edge = partial, dashed box = stubbed or planned. To change a box's status, copy a box of the style you want. Point at the dashed boxes yourself before a judge does.

slides.title: [The hardest choice you made]
slides.notes: 0:45. Pick a decision where the alternative was genuinely tempting. 'We tried X first and measured Y' is the strongest form.

slides.title: [The scenario: a real user doing a real task]
steps: [Step 1: what you click and what the audience sees]
[Step 3: the moment that shows it works]
slides.fallback: [Recorded video or screenshots: file name and where it is]
slides.notes: 2:30. Rehearse the exact click path. Use a demo account and data that can't fail. Have the recording open in another window before you start.

slides.title: [What the numbers say, as a sentence]
slides.footnote: [Method and baseline: how each number was measured and what you compare it to]
slides.notes: 1:00. No number without a method and a baseline. If a number is weak, show it anyway and explain it. Don't fill the slide with vanity numbers.

slides.eyebrow: Did we hit what we set at intake?
slides.title: Milestones: planned vs. achieved
slides.notes: 0:45. Copy criteria word for word from your intake proposal. Status cells: PASSED (black), MISSED or STOPPED (red), PARTIAL (grey), PENDING (white). A missed milestone told honestly is a finding.

slides.title: What broke, and what we learned

cards.title: [Failure or limit]
cards.body: [When it happens and how bad it is]

cards.title: [Failure or limit]
cards.body: [When it happens and how bad it is]

slides.notes: 0:45. Judges trust a team that names its own weak spots.

slides.title: Team and contributions
slides.notes: 0:45. Recruiters and sponsors are in the room. 'Built the ingestion pipeline' tells them more than 'passionate engineer'. Asks must be answerable today.

slides.title: [Next goal: continue, pivot, or stop]
slides.body: [What you will build next, or why you are stopping]
slides.cta: [What you want the audience to do]
slides.notes: 0:30. End on one clear call to action, then open for questions.
